newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kirch, Canal-plus map out European pay-TV - report.
newsitem.headline: Kirch, Canal-plus map out European pay-TV - report.

text.p: Munich media mogul Leo Kirch and France's Canal Plus are planning to carve up the European pay-TV market between themselves, the news weekly Der Spiegel reported on Saturday.
Kirch would agree to limit his activities to Germany if Canal Plus stayed of his way, the magazine said.

Kirch would reduce his 45 percent stake in Italy's Telepiu, allowing Canal Plus to boost its 45 percent stake to a majority. He would also abandon his search for a partner to enter the Spanish market, it said.
In exchange, Canal Plus would sell its stake in German pay-TV station Premiere to Kirch, boosting his stake from 25 percent to 50 percent, matching the share held by Bertelsmann.
Marketing Premiere together with Kirch's DF1 would give new impetus to DF1, the magazine quoted Michel Thoulouze, head of foreign business for Canal-plus, as saying.
But Bertelsmann is likely to oppose the plan, as it has the right of first refusal to Canal-plus's Premiere stake, the magazine said.
